details.notice: The published origin answers use kommen + aus + country name.

ruleSteps.notice: Use aus before the published country expression.

details.notice: Use du in the taught informal patterns and capitalized Sie with the formal verb form.

ruleSteps.model: Wie heißt du? · Wie heißen Sie?
ruleSteps.notice: Keep pronoun and verb form in the same register.

details.notice: Lesson 2 extends present conjugation to wir, ihr, sie and formal Sie.

ruleSteps.model: wir sind · ihr seid · sie/Sie sind
ruleSteps.notice: Match each pronoun with its published present form.

details.notice: In the taught statements, the finite verb is in second position.

ruleSteps.notice: Build person + finite verb + complement.

details.notice: Use nicht in the taught profile statements to negate a state or description.

ruleSteps.notice: Place nicht with the taught statement pattern.

details.notice: German finite verbs agree with the person: ich, du, er/sie/es, wir, ihr, sie and formal Sie.

ruleSteps.model: ich heiße · du heißt · Sie heißen
ruleSteps.notice: Choose the pronoun first, then the matching finite verb form.

details.notice: Published present forms include regular endings and the taught special paradigms heißen and sein.

ruleSteps.notice: Regular forms use a verb stem plus the person ending.
In heißen, du and er/sie/es use heißt.

ruleSteps.model: ich bin · du bist · Sie sind
ruleSteps.notice: Learn the irregular forms of sein as whole forms.

details.notice: The taught patterns contrast profession after sein with arbeiten als, bei or in.

ruleSteps.notice: After sein, use the taught profession without an article.
Use arbeiten als before a profession.
Use bei or in only in the published workplace patterns.

details.notice: Published profession pairs form feminine person words with -in where evidenced; plural -innen is used only when stored in the source.

ruleSteps.notice: Link each published feminine form to its masculine base; preserve source-supported stem changes.
Use -innen only for a source-published feminine plural.

details.notice: A taught W-question starts with the question word, followed by the finite verb and the person.

ruleSteps.model: Wie heißt du? · Woher kommen Sie?
ruleSteps.notice: Use W-word + finite verb + person + complement.
